By Hon’ble Shri A.K.Bhardwaj, Member (J)
Indubitable facts of the case are that the applicant
herein initially joined the Military Engineering Services
(MES) as Mazdoor w.e.f. 03.04.1995 and is presently
working in the office of Garrison Engineer (AF), Subroto
Park, Delhi Cantt-110010. It is not disputed that he
appeared in the Trade Test for the post of Mate Pipe
Fitter on 17.3.2005 and was declared qualified.
Instruction to this effect was published vide GE (AF)
Subroto Park PTO No.17/25/2007 dated 23.04.2007.
It is the case of the applicant that when certain other
individuals who had not passed the trade test for the
post of Mate Pipe Fitter and had passed the trade test
for some other category such as Mate (FGM) have been
given promotion as Mate Pipe Fitter, those who had
passed the trade test for mate (P.F) have not been so
promoted.
2. The stand taken by the respondents in their counter
reply is that the individuals given promotion as Mate
had passed the trade test in the year 1999. Para 4.4 of
reply of the respondents read thus:

3 OA-838/2012
“The Individuals had passed the
Trade Test in the year 1999 and
during that period the policy letter
supplied to the applicant vide HQ
Chief Engineer Western Command
letter No.30674/RTI/GEN/1873/E1C(1)
dated 17 July 2010 is not an authority
or the policy letter issued much later
passing the trade test by the applicant
as well as other individuals.”
3. When it is not clear from the reply filed on behalf
of the respondents that for which category the
individuals referred to in para 4.6 of the reply passed
the trade test, we find that in terms of order dated
29.07.2013, HQ WAC Palam,Delhi Cantt. had intimated
that MES 505159 Shri Mohinder Singh Chow had
passed the Trade Test held on 18/19.01.1999 and
S/Shri Som Dutt ,Krishan Lal and Man Phool Singh had
passed the trade test on 18/19.01.1999, 15.06.1999
etc. From the letter it is apparent that Shri Man Phool
Singh had passed the trade test for Mate (Elect) but it
is not clear that for which trade S/Shri Kishan Lal, M
Singh and Som Dutt had passed trade test. Issue
regarding passing the trade test by Sh. Shankar Lal is
under investigation. The relevant excerpt of the
communication dated 29.7.2013 (ibid) read thus:-
“(i)Srl No.1:- MES-311653 Sh. Ram
Kishor, S/wala was not served with this area
is existing period, he has served with GE(AF)
Halwara at that time. The entries for passing

found is his service book. The enquiry in this
regard has already been initiated with GE(AF)
Halwara i.e. date of passing of trade test and
copies of PTOs vide this office letter No.
1050/TT/39/E10 dt. 15 Jul 2013 as and when
such info received from GE(AF) Halwara, the
same will be fwd to your HQ. However, the
individual has promoted to Mate category as
per your HQ Part II order No.42/01/2010 dt.
18 Oct. 2010.
(ii) Srl No.2:- MES-312728 Sh.Hukum Singh,

No.37/17/2001.

Mate held on 18/19.01.1999 on first attempt
vide GE (AF) Subrota Park PTO
No.40/01/2005.
(iv) Srl No.4:- MES-370270 Sh.Som Dutt,
Chow has passed the Trade test of Mate held
on 18/19.01.1999 on first attempt vide GE
(AF) Subrota Park PTO No.40/02/2005.
(v) Srl No.5:- MES-370694 Sh.Shankar
Lal,Maz passed the Trade test of Masson,
matter is under investigation is in hand and
report will be fwd in due course.
(vi) Srl No.6:- NO-1087 Sh.Kishan Lal,Maz
passed the Trade test of Mate (P/Ftr.), vide
PTO No.15/06/99.
(vii) Srl No.7:- MES-371672 Sh.Kul Bhushan,
Maz passed the Trade test of Mate (P/Ftr.),
vide PTO No.09/98/99.
(viii) Srl No.8:- MES-360664 Sh.Man Phool
Singh,Maz passed the Trade test of Mate
(Elct). Matter is under investigation is in hand
and report will be fwd in due course.”

5 OA-838/2012
4. When in para 4.6 of the OA the applicants have given the
details of the individuals, who had not passed the test in P.F.
trade and were promoted as Mate Pipe Fitter, the only plea
taken in para 4.6 of the reply is that the allegations made by
the applicant are baseless. The stand taken in para-4.6 of
the OA is not in consonance with the letter dated
29.07.2013. From the said letter it is apparent that the
category for which S/Sh. Hukum Singh, Mohinder Singh and
Som Dutt had passed the Trade test is not clear. In terms
of the Circular no 30233/TIP/344/EIC-II dated 15.6.1993,
it is clarified that the incumbents of the posts
Mazdoor/Chowkidar/Safaiwala which are the feeder
categories for various semi-skilled categories can opt only
one trade test of his choice for promotion. The contents of
the circular read thus:-
“it is clarified that the
Mazdoor/Chowkidar/Safaiwala which are the
feeder categories for various semi-skilled
may be allowed to appear in trade test of his
choice for more than trade (semi-skilled).
However, only one trade of his choice in
which he wants to earn promotion. Once he
decided his line of trade and accepts
promotion in semi-skilled, he will not be
allowed to have further option at skilled
level.”
5. It is not in disputed that in terms of
Recruitment Rules for the post of Mate Pipe
Fitter (Annexure A/2) Mazdoor / Chowkidar/ Safaiwala

6 OA-838/2012
are eligible for promotion to the post of Mate Pipe Fitter.

6. Once the applicant who had passed the trade test for the
post Mate Pipe Fitter could have opted only for one trade,
the respondents should have considered him for promotion
against the vacancies in the category for which he passed
the trade test. Though in view of the law declared by
Hon’ble Supreme Court in B. S. Wajwa & Anr. Vs. State
of Punjab & Ors., JT 1998 (1) SC 57, at this belated stage
we may not interfere with promotion of the respondent
nos.8 to 10 but at the same time we may not be oblivious of
the fact that the incumbents of the feeder category could
have choosen only one trade and once the applicant had
passed the test for the trade Pipe Fitter, he had a right

7 OA-838/2012
to be considered for next promotion in the trade ahead of
those who passed the tests in different trades.
7. In the wake, the OA is disposed with the direction to
the respondents to consider the applicant for his promotion
to the post of Mate Pipe Fitter within a period of 8 weeks’
from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. No costs.
(K.N. Shrivastava) (A. K. Bhardwaj)
